attempts.summary: Configured PostgreSQL 13 streaming replication across node1 (primary), node2, and node3 (standbys) on AlmaLinux 9, secured with a self-signed CA (CN=postgres-cluster-ca) created on node1. Per-node server certs (CN=node1/node2/node3) and a replicator client cert (CN=replicator) were issued by that CA and distributed. pg_hba.conf on all nodes restricts replication to hostssl entries requiring `cert` auth (clientcert=verify-full implied), so only peers presenting a CA-issued client cert can replicate; plaintext and foreign-CA-signed connections were proven to fail. Standbys were built via pg_basebackup -R over TLS (sslmode=verify-full) and are streaming with TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384. Ran the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol (standbys first, primary last), proving changed boot IDs on every node and confirming post-restart replication/data recovery, including a live write on the primary after its own restart.
